abstract.para: curl (and its underlying library, libcurl) is an essential command-line utility and library for transferring data with URLs across multiple network protocols. It is widely used by core system utilities, administrative scripts and enterprise software stacks across &suselinux;.

topic.para: The curl package follows the Stable lifecycle model. It is maintained and supported according to the following rules:

listitem.para: Even when curl packages receive version updates, &suse; guarantees complete ABI stability. Upstream curl strictly adheres to backward compatibility, ensuring that existing applications, system utilities and third-party software linked against libcurl continue to function reliably without requiring recompilation across &suselinux; &productnumber;.

curl is not updated on a regular or fixed calendar schedule. Instead, version updates are triggered on demand when a substantial number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) accumulate upstream or when the technical complexity of backporting patches across all active codestreams recommends a version update.

Due to the high frequency of upstream CVEs and the potential fragility of backporting complex security patches to older codebases, delivering validated newer versions provides robust security fixes while maintaining enterprise stability.

Updating curl to a newer stable upstream version to resolve complex CVE sets while strictly preserving API/ABI compatibility is an established practice successfully used across previous &suselinux; releases.
